turns.en: You don't really know that you don't know anything. You're just figuring it out. One great way to start is to pick something you think is great, something you like, and throw it into Sketch or Figma and recreate it. Just by going through the motion of laying out elements on the screen or on a page, you slowly learn about padding and alignment. You realize, oh yeah, all these things are aligned here. By the act of recreating things you like, you learn those things. It's a bit like the idea that if you force yourself to smile, you feel happier. If you're really sad or in a bad place, force yourself to laugh and smile. Even if it's fake, the act of doing it actually makes you feel slightly better. It's a little like that. You're not designing the screen, you're tracing over it. You're recreating it, but the act of doing it makes you learn things. Some of it sticks.
turns.zh: 你其实并不知道自己什么都不知道，你只是在摸索。一个好的入门方法是挑一件你觉得很棒、你喜欢的东西，把它丢进 Sketch 或 Figma 里照着重做。仅仅是动手把元素排布在屏幕或页面上，你就在慢慢理解内边距和对齐，然后你会想：哦对，这些东西在这里是对齐的。通过重现你喜欢的东西，你确实学到了那些东西。这有点像那个说法：如果你强迫自己微笑，你会真的感觉更开心。如果你现在很难过、状态很差，逼自己笑一笑，哪怕那是假的，但做出这个动作本身会让你好受一点，让人开心一点点。学设计也是类似。你不是在设计屏幕，你只是在描摹它、重做它，但这个动作会让你学到东西，而且有些会留下来。

turns.en: Instead of telling you, if you have an idea, just do it, it's more useful to put yourself in a state where, when you see these little interactions from other products or other people, you make a note of it. Like, oh yeah, I was using Red's thing, I hovered and got a little wave emoji. That was nice, that was cute. Whatever emotion it is, make a note. Save it somewhere. Maybe create a folder where you save screenshots, or use Apple Notes and just write it down. I remember reading a blog post years ago. I forget exactly when. It was a really nice piece, and at the end it had the author's signature, a vector signature. I remember thinking, that's so cool. You don't see that anywhere else on the page—no other handwriting or anything—but the signature is cool. So guess what? For one of my first side projects, an Apple Watch game called Break the Safe, I wrote a case study of it, a long piece of writing, which I don't usually do. And at the end, I converted my signature to a vector and threw it in there. Because a little detail is nice. Be on the lookout. When you're browsing through Twitter or wherever, we're exposed to so much good work. When some piece makes you think, oh, this is cool, just make a note, save it. Then next time you're doing something similar, you'll remember. Next time I was writing a blog post, I thought, you know what, I remember someone had a signature and it felt classy. I'll do that.
turns.zh: 与其告诉你“如果你有个想法，就去做”，更有用的做法是让自己进入一种状态：当你看到其他产品、其他人身上的这些小交互时，你会记一笔。比如“哦，我在用 Red 家的东西，鼠标悬停时出现了一个小波浪表情，真好玩，真可爱。”不管是什么感受，记下来。把它存到某个地方，也许建一个文件夹存截图，或者在 Apple Notes 里写下来。我记得很多年前读过一篇博客，具体什么时候忘了。那是一篇很好的文章，结尾有作者的签名，一个矢量签名。我当时觉得：太酷了。页面上其他地方都没有手写笔迹之类的东西，就这个签名很酷。结果你猜怎么着？在我最早的一个业余项目里——一个叫 Break the Safe 的 Apple Watch 游戏——我给它写了一个案例研究。那是个很长的文章，我平时不怎么写，但在结尾我把自己的签名转成矢量放了进去。因为一个小细节就很棒。要留意观察。当你刷 Twitter 或别的什么，我们会接触到大量好作品。当某件作品让你觉得“哦，这个很酷”，就记下来、存下来。这样下次你遇到类似的事情时就会想起来。我下次写博客时就想：“你知道吗，我记得有人加了签名，显得很优雅，我也要这样。”

turns.en: Rafa, I think we could talk for hours. I genuinely enjoyed everything about this conversation. In a world where so much of the discourse is about robots, scale, efficiency, and all the new technology, this was a very human conversation. I appreciated every part of it, and your perspective is life-giving and enjoyable. Thank you for taking the time today.
turns.zh: Rafa，我觉得我们可以聊好几个小时。我真的很享受这场对话的每一个部分。在这样一个充满关于机器人、规模、效率和各种新技术的讨论的世界里，这是一场非常有人情味的对话。我很珍惜这次交流，你的观点让人觉得充满生命力、很愉快。谢谢你今天抽出时间。

turns.en: Thank you. This was a blast. Love talking to you. Thanks for having me.
turns.zh: 谢谢你。这太开心了。很喜欢和你聊天。感谢你的邀请。

consensus.en: Software should make people feel something; emotional experiences are more memorable than efficient workflows.
consensus.zh: 软件应该让人产生情感共鸣；情感化的体验比高效流程更令人难忘。

consensus.en: Small delightful details and humanity in software—surprise, humor, personality—create connection with users.
consensus.zh: 软件中充满惊喜、幽默和个性的人性化细节，能与用户建立连接。

consensus.en: Designers should present ideas through short entertaining videos that sell the concept, not just share mockups.
consensus.zh: 设计师应通过简短有趣的视频来推销概念，而不是只分享静态稿。

consensus.en: Side projects free designers from pressure, letting them inject personal expression and take creative risks.
consensus.zh: 个人项目让设计师摆脱压力，注入个人表达并承担创作风险。

consensus.en: Pay attention to delightful interactions in other products and save them as inspiration for your own work.
consensus.zh: 留意其他产品中的精彩交互并保存下来，作为自己工作的灵感。

consensus.en: Trust users to handle unfamiliar patterns; over-optimizing for edge cases lowers the ceiling of experience.
consensus.zh: 相信用户能适应不熟悉的模式；过度优化边缘场景会降低体验上限。

contrarian.en: Losing 20–30% of sign-ups to an emotional onboarding video is acceptable if it builds deeper connection.
contrarian.zh: 为一段情感化引导视频牺牲20–30%注册量是值得的，如果它能建立更深的连接。

contrarian.en: Big companies can't take bold design risks; smaller teams and indie developers are the ones who can.
contrarian.zh: 大公司无法承担大胆的设计风险；小团队和独立开发者才能做到。

contrarian.en: Adding intentional friction can create a stronger emotional impact—frustration can lead to memorable moments.
contrarian.zh: 故意增加摩擦能带来更强的情绪冲击——适度的挫败感可以造就难忘时刻。

contrarian.en: Design for a specific persona and accept losing others; generalizing too much makes the experience bland.
contrarian.zh: 为特定用户群设计并接受他人流失；过度泛化会让体验变得平庸。

contrarian.en: Removing familiar UI affordances like the home indicator is a good bet—people will figure it out.
contrarian.zh: 移除主屏幕指示器等熟悉的UI元素是明智的——用户会自己弄明白。

contrarian.en: Humor and 'wouldn't it be funny' moments are legitimate design tools, not unprofessional distractions.
contrarian.zh: 幽默和‘这样是不是很有趣’的瞬间是正当的设计工具，而非不专业的干扰。
